item.title: Russia’s war in Ukraine puts Europe on edge
item.description:
President Donald Trump is easing some of the economic pressure on Russia in hopes of bringing Vladimir Putin closer to a peace deal — a gamble that will test whether economic incentives can move Moscow where years of sanctions have not. The administration's decision to temporarily ease restrictions on Russian diesel has drawn opposition from Republicans on Capitol Hill and skepticism over whether the move will meaningfully lower prices for Americans. Meanwhile, Russia has offered few public signs of concessions in return. Six Republican senators joined Democrats this week in urging Trump to reverse the decision, while five House Republicans signed a separate bipartisan letter Thursday seeking to revoke the Treasury authorization. item.title: Paris left reeling as student-led protests turn chaotic
item.description:

A march in central Milan on Saturday to protest against rising living costs began peacefully but ended with masked rioters throwing stones, paving blocks and other objects at riot police and setting fire to barricades made from bar tables. item.title: Oregon father is the latest armed civilian to confront a gunman in a U.S. mass shooting
item.description:
A teacher threw her cellphone at a teenage gunman and tackled him during Thursday’s deadly shooting at an Oregon elementary school, fighting to wrestle away his shotgun before an armed father shot him dead, police revealed Friday . The 16-year-old gunman killed four people, including three children, at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon, where he had previously been a special needs student. All of the victims were in a special-needs classroom, school officials said. The teacher was not injured in the confrontation. Her heroic actions “almost certainly helped prevent more bloodshed,” Bend Police Chief Mike Krantz said during a news conference detailing the attack. The father, identified as Kaylub Giamanco , 36, has two children at the school. He witnessed the initial shooting outside and followed the gunman into the school, police said. item.title: Sudan army accused of drone strike on livestock market
item.description:
Survivors of the Abu Shandi drone strike at Ad-Damazin Teaching Hospital, in Blue Nile State, Sudan, on October 12, 2026. Photo by Eisa Dafalla. AD-DAMAZIN, Sudan—On the morning of October 9, Ahmed Ragab Abu Shina, 39, joined dozens of other displaced people digging for gold in a seasonal riverbed, known locally as a khor , near the Abu Shandi shelter in Sudan’s Blue Nile State. At around 9 a.m., a drone flew overhead from the south. No one knew whose it was, and no one thought it had come for them. Suddenly, an explosive shell landed in the middle of the khor , where men, women and children were working side by side. “After the shell fell, dozens went down, and whoever could flee fled,” Ragab told Drop Site News. “In those moments, no one knew where their family members or relatives were.” The strike killed 32 displaced people—26 women, four children and two elderly people—and wounded…
